auth_header: Authorization: Bearer <OPENAI_API_KEY> (env OPENAI_API_KEY). Optional scoping headers: "OpenAI-Organization: <org id>" and "OpenAI-Project: <project id>" (only needed for legacy user keys that belong to multiple orgs/projects; project-scoped keys don't need them). Admin endpoints need a separate Admin API key. Key changes propagate in ~15 min; revocations in seconds.
chat_endpoint: Two live text endpoints: (1) POST /v1/responses — the recommended one for all new projects and REQUIRED for tool calling on gpt-6-astra ("Chat Completions does not support function calling with GPT-6 Astra"). Body: {model, input: string | Item[], instructions?, tools?, tool_choice?, parallel_tool_calls?, text?: {format, verbosity}, reasoning?: {effort, summary}, max_output_tokens?, stream?, store? (default true, 30-day retention), previous_response_id?, conversation?, include?, background?, truncation?, service_tier?, prompt_cache_key?, metadata?}. Response: {id: "resp_...", status: "in_progress"|"completed"|"incomplete", output: Item[] (types message | function_call | reasoning | custom_tool_call | ...), output_text (SDK helper), usage, incomplete_details: {reason: "max_output_tokens"|"max_messages"|"content_filter"|"steered"}, error}. (2) POST /v1/chat/completions — still supported (OpenAI-compatible shape used by most other providers). Body: {model, messages[{role: "developer"|"system"|"user"|"assistant"|"tool", content, name?, tool_calls?, tool_call_id?}], tools?, tool_choice?, parallel_tool_calls?, response_format?, max_completion_tokens? (max_tokens is DEPRECATED), reasoning_effort?, verbosity?, stream?, stream_options?: {include_usage}, store?, metadata?, service_tier?, prompt_cache_key?, temperature?, top_p?, n?, stop?, seed?, logprobs?, top_logprobs?}. Response: {id, object: "chat.completion", created, model, choices[{index, message{role, content, tool_calls, refusal, annotations}, finish_reason: "stop"|"length"|"tool_calls"|"content_filter"|"function_call", logprobs}], usage, service_tier, system_fingerprint}. Assistants API was sunset Aug 26 2026.
list_models_endpoint: GET /v1/models → {object: "list", data: Model[]}; GET /v1/models/{model} → single Model. Model object fields: id (string, the id you pass as `model`), object: "model", created (unix seconds), owned_by (string), shutdown_date (string|null, set once a deprecation is announced). The list is NOT filtered to chat-capable models (includes embeddings, tts, whisper, dall-e, moderation, fine-tunes, dated snapshots) and carries NO context window, max output, modality, capability or pricing metadata — you must maintain a static catalogue keyed by id/prefix for those. Current flagship ids (Sep 2026): gpt-6-astra (1.05M ctx / 128K out, cutoff Apr 30 2026), gpt-5.6-sol (alias gpt-5.6), gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna (all 1.05M ctx / 128K out, cutoff Feb 16 2026); older still-served ids include gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro, gpt-5.4(-mini/-nano), gpt-5, gpt-5-mini, gpt-5.3-codex, gpt-4.1(-mini), gpt-4o, o3, o4-mini.
model_fields: id: string; object: "model"; created: number (unix s); owned_by: string (e.g. "openai", "system", or your org for fine-tunes); shutdown_date?: string|null. Nothing else — no context_length, pricing, supported_parameters, modalities or capability flags (contrast OpenRouter). Per-model pages at developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/<id> expose context window, max output tokens, knowledge cutoff, supported endpoints (Chat Completions / Responses / Batch), supported features (streaming, structured_outputs, function_calling, prompt_caching, image_input, web_search, file_search), modalities, allowed reasoning-effort values, per-1M pricing and per-tier RPM/TPM — but only as HTML, not JSON.
pricing_source: No machine-readable pricing API. Human pages only: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (canonical) and https://openai.com/api/pricing/ , plus each model card. Per-1M-token USD (input / cached input / output), standard tier, Sep 2026: gpt-6-astra 10 / 1 / 50; gpt-5.6-sol 4 / 0.40 / 20; gpt-5.6-terra 2 / 0.20 / 12; gpt-5.6-luna 0.20 / 0.02 / 1.20; gpt-5.5 5 / 0.50 / 30; gpt-5.5-pro 30 / — / 180; gpt-5.4 2.50 / 0.25 / 15; gpt-5.4-mini 0.75 / 0.075 / 4.50; gpt-5.4-nano 0.20 / 0.02 / 1.25; gpt-5 1.25 / 0.125 / 10; gpt-5-mini 0.25 / 0.025 / 2; gpt-5.3-codex 1.75 / 0.175 / 14; gpt-4.1 2 / 0.50 / 8; gpt-4.1-mini 0.40 / 0.10 / 1.60; gpt-4o 2.50 / 1.25 / 10; o3 2 / 0.50 / 8; o4-mini 1.10 / 0.275 / 4.40. Cached input = 0.1x uncached on current models (0.5x on gpt-4.1/gpt-4o/o-series). Batch API and "flex" service_tier = 50% off; "fast" service_tier = 2x; "priority" tier is a premium. Reasoning tokens are billed as OUTPUT tokens. Hard-code a table keyed by model-id prefix and refresh manually; compute cost client-side from usage.
quirks: Two APIs with different shapes: Chat Completions (messages/response_format/max_completion_tokens/reasoning_effort/nested tools) vs Responses (input+instructions/text.format/max_output_tokens/reasoning.effort/flat tools). gpt-6-astra tool calling ONLY works on /v1/responses; Chat Completions is kept for compatibility but 'Responses is recommended for all new projects'.

max_tokens is deprecated on Chat Completions — send max_completion_tokens (Responses: max_output_tokens). The limit INCLUDES hidden reasoning tokens; OpenAI recommends reserving >=25,000 for reasoning+output when experimenting with reasoning models, and finish_reason 'length' / status 'incomplete' with incomplete_details.reason 'max_output_tokens' means the budget was eaten by reasoning.

System prompt placement: Chat Completions accepts role 'system' or 'developer' (developer is the reasoning-model-era name; both accepted). Responses uses top-level `instructions`, and `instructions` is NOT carried over by previous_response_id — resend it every turn.

Sampling params are rejected (HTTP 400) on reasoning/GPT-5.x+ models: temperature, top_p, top_logprobs are unsupported; logprobs unsupported in Chat Completions; 'message.output_text.logprobs' unsupported in Responses include. Do not send temperature by default — only for legacy gpt-4o/gpt-4.1.

tool_choice specific-function syntax differs: Chat Completions {"type":"function","function":{"name":"x"}} vs Responses {"type":"function","name":"x"}. Both accept strings 'auto' | 'required' | 'none' and the object {"type":"allowed_tools","mode":"auto"|"required","tools":[...]}.

Strict schemas: `strict: true` requires additionalProperties:false on every object, every property listed in `required` (optional fields modelled as type ["string","null"]), root must be an object, no pattern/minLength/maxLength/minimum/maximum, anyOf only of single-schema refs, $defs/$ref and recursion OK. Chat Completions tools are non-strict by default; Responses tries to normalize schemas into strict mode and falls back to non-strict if it can't — so arguments may be invalid JSON when strict is off; always try/catch JSON.parse.

Reasoning items must be replayed: with reasoning models, every `reasoning` item returned alongside function_call items must be passed back in the next request's input together with the function_call and function_call_output items (or a 400 follows). Stateless (store:false) responses include reasoning.encrypted_content automatically; keep and replay the entire output array. Persisted reasoning is reusable only within the same model family.

State/storage: Responses are stored by default (store defaults true, 30-day retention, retrievable via GET /v1/responses/{id}); set store:false for privacy, which also disables previous_response_id chaining. All prior-turn tokens are re-billed as input on each chained request.

Prompt caching is automatic (prefix match, >=1024 tokens); cached tokens show in usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens (Chat) / usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens (Responses). Route with `prompt_cache_key` (replaces deprecated `user`). Retention: gpt-5.6+ use prompt_cache_options:{ttl:"30m"} (only value); older models use prompt_cache_retention 'in_memory' | '24h' (deprecated on new models).

reasoning effort value set is model-specific: gpt-5.6 family accepts none|low|medium(default)|high|xhigh|max; gpt-6-astra REJECTS 'none' (400) — use 'low'; older gpt-5/5.4 accept minimal|low|medium|high. Validate per model before sending.
verbosity is top-level `verbosity` in Chat Completions but nested `text.verbosity` in Responses (low|medium|high).
service_tier: 'auto'|'default'|'flex'|'scale'|'priority'|'fast'; invalid values return 400; gpt-6-astra rejects 'fast'/'priority' under EU data residency. Response echoes the tier actually used.

Structured-output refusals arrive in a separate `refusal` field (Chat: choices[].message.refusal; Responses: message content part type 'refusal', streamed as response.refusal.delta) instead of the JSON body — check it before parsing. First request with a new schema has extra latency (schema compiled and cached).

Streaming usage is opt-in on Chat Completions: without stream_options:{include_usage:true} you get no usage at all; with it, a trailing chunk with choices: [] and a usage object arrives before data: [DONE]. Responses streaming always includes usage in the terminal response.completed event.

Error envelope is {error:{message,type,param,code}}. 429 is ambiguous: distinguish error.code 'rate_limit_exceeded'/'slow_down' (retry after Retry-After) from 'insufficient_quota'/'credit_balance_exhausted' (billing — do not retry). 503 code 'server_is_overloaded' — back off.

GET /v1/models returns every model type (embeddings, tts, whisper, dall-e, moderation, snapshots) with no capability metadata; filter by id prefix (gpt-, o3, o4, chatgpt-) and exclude -realtime, -audio, -transcribe, -tts, -search, -embedding, -image, -moderation to build a chat picker.
Model aliases (e.g. gpt-5.6 → gpt-5.6-sol) silently move to newer snapshots; pin dated snapshot ids for reproducibility; `shutdown_date` on the model object flags announced deprecations.
TPM accounting uses max(max_completion_tokens, estimated prompt tokens) — a huge max_completion_tokens can trip 429 on TPM even for short prompts.
rate_limit_headers: x-ratelimit-limit-requests, x-ratelimit-limit-tokens, x-ratelimit-remaining-requests, x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens, x-ratelimit-reset-requests, x-ratelimit-reset-tokens (reset values are Go-style durations, e.g. "1s", "6m0s", "20ms"). On 429 a Retry-After header (seconds) is present — wait at least that long. Limits are per-org, per-model, RPM+TPM (plus RPD on some tiers) and rise with usage tier (Free, Tier 1–5; e.g. gpt-5.6-sol Tier 1 = 500 RPM / 500K TPM, Tier 5 = 15,000 RPM / 40M TPM). TPM check counts max(max_completion_tokens, estimated request tokens).
reasoning_params: Responses: `reasoning: {effort: "none"|"minimal"|"low"|"medium"|"high"|"xhigh"|"max", summary: "auto"|"concise"|"detailed", context?: "auto"|"current_turn"|"all_turns"}`; default effort "medium". Chat Completions: top-level `reasoning_effort` with the same value set (no summaries available). Allowed values are model-specific — gpt-5.6 family: none|low|medium|high|xhigh|max; gpt-6-astra: low|medium|high|xhigh|max (no "none"); gpt-5/5.4 era: minimal|low|medium|high. Reasoning tokens are hidden, billed as output, and reported in usage.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens (Responses) / usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens (Chat). Summaries stream as response.reasoning_summary_text.delta and appear in the reasoning item's `summary[]`. For stateless use add include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"] (automatic when store:false) and replay reasoning items across tool-call turns. No explicit thinking-token budget — control via max_output_tokens (reserve ≥25k).
streaming: Both endpoints: set `stream: true`; server-sent events over HTTP. Responses API emits typed events, each with a `type` and monotonically increasing `sequence_number`: response.created, response.in_progress, response.output_item.added, response.content_part.added, response.output_text.delta, response.output_text.done, response.refusal.delta/.done, response.function_call_arguments.delta, response.function_call_arguments.done, response.reasoning_summary_text.delta, response.reasoning_text.delta, response.content_part.done, response.output_item.done, then exactly one terminal event response.completed | response.incomplete | response.failed (each carrying the full Response object including `usage`), or `error`. Tool-call args: concatenate function_call_arguments.delta per output_index until .done. Chat Completions emits `data: {object: "chat.completion.chunk", choices:[{index, delta:{role?, content?, tool_calls?:[{index, id?, type?, function:{name?, arguments}}], refusal?}, finish_reason}]}` lines terminated by `data: [DONE]`; usage is null on every chunk unless stream_options:{include_usage:true}, which adds one final chunk with choices: [] and the usage object. Optional stream_options.include_obfuscation. `background: true` (Responses) lets you poll/resume long runs instead of holding the stream.
structured_output: Responses: `text: {format: {type: "json_schema", name: "<name>", schema: {...}, strict: true}}` (also type "json_object" and "text"). Chat Completions: `response_format: {type: "json_schema", json_schema: {name, schema, strict: true}}`, or {type:"json_object"} (legacy JSON mode — you must also say "JSON" in the prompt). Strict-mode rules: root is an object; every object has additionalProperties:false; every property is in `required` (use type ["T","null"] for optional); supported types string/number/integer/boolean/array/object/null/enum; unsupported keywords pattern/minLength/maxLength/minimum/maximum (and other format validators); anyOf allowed only over single-schema alternatives; $defs + $ref and recursion allowed. Result text is in message content (Responses: output_text / message content part output_text) and is guaranteed valid JSON under strict; a `refusal` field/part is returned instead when the model declines. First use of a schema adds latency (server-side compilation, then cached). Function tools support the same `strict: true` for guaranteed-valid arguments. Supported on gpt-4o and every later model; recommended default model gpt-6-astra.
tools_format: Responses API (flat, internally tagged): tools: [{type: "function", name, description, parameters: <JSON Schema object>, strict?: bool}] plus hosted tools {type: "web_search"}, {type:"file_search", vector_store_ids}, {type:"code_interpreter"}, {type:"mcp", server_label, server_url, ...}, {type:"computer"}, {type:"image_generation"}, {type:"shell"}, {type:"apply_patch"}, {type:"custom", name, description, format?: {type:"grammar", syntax:"lark"|"regex", definition}} (free-text tool input, returned as custom_tool_call.input), and {type:"namespace"} / defer_loading:true for tool search. Model returns output items {type:"function_call", id, call_id, name, arguments: "<json string>", status}; you reply by appending {type:"function_call_output", call_id, output: "<string>"} (plus the returned reasoning items) to `input`. tool_choice: "auto"|"required"|"none" | {type:"function", name} | {type:"allowed_tools", mode:"auto"|"required", tools:[{type:"function",name}...]} | {type:"web_search"} etc. parallel_tool_calls: bool (default true). Chat Completions (nested, externally tagged): tools: [{type:"function", function:{name, description, parameters, strict?}}]; assistant message carries tool_calls: [{id, type:"function", function:{name, arguments:"<json string>"}}]; reply with {role:"tool", tool_call_id, content}; tool_choice: "auto"|"required"|"none" | {type:"function", function:{name}} | {type:"allowed_tools", ...}. Streaming: Responses → response.output_item.added / response.function_call_arguments.delta / .done; Chat → delta.tool_calls[] keyed by `index`, accumulate `function.arguments`. Chat Completions tool calling is NOT available for gpt-6-astra.
usage_and_cost_in_response: Token counts yes, dollar cost NO — OpenAI never returns cost; compute it client-side from usage × the static price table. Chat Completions `usage`: {prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, prompt_tokens_details: {cached_tokens, cache_write_tokens, text_tokens, image_tokens, audio_tokens}, completion_tokens_details: {reasoning_tokens, text_tokens, audio_tokens, accepted_prediction_tokens, rejected_prediction_tokens}}. Responses `usage`: {input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, input_tokens_details: {cached_tokens}, output_tokens_details: {reasoning_tokens}}. Billing formula: (input_tokens − cached_tokens) × input_rate + cached_tokens × cached_rate + output_tokens × output_rate (output_tokens already includes reasoning_tokens; don't double count). Streaming: Chat requires stream_options.include_usage for the trailing usage chunk; Responses delivers usage inside response.completed/incomplete/failed. `service_tier` is echoed in the response so you can apply flex (0.5x) / fast (2x) multipliers.

base_url: https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1  (OpenAI-compatible; pass as OpenAI SDK base_url). Variants: https://us.api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1 for US-only serverless router models (1.5x price); Anthropic-compatible base is https://api.fireworks.ai/inference (SDK appends /v1/messages); control-plane (model catalogue) is https://api.fireworks.ai/v1
auth_header: Authorization: Bearer <FIREWORKS_API_KEY>  (env var name in official docs: FIREWORKS_API_KEY; plus Content-Type: application/json). Bearer is the only documented scheme — no x-api-key, no query-param key, and the Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages endpoint also uses Bearer with no anthropic-version header. Unauthenticated calls return HTTP 401 with envelope {"error":{"message","param","code":"UNAUTHORIZED","type":"error"},"request_id"}.
chat_endpoint: POST https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1/chat/completions  (GET returns 405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED; also POST /inference/v1/completions, POST /inference/v1/messages (Anthropic-compatible), POST /inference/v1/responses (beta OpenAI Responses API with MCP tools), POST /inference/v1/embeddings)
streaming: stream: true -> Server-Sent Events, each event `data: {ChatCompletionStreamResponse}` with choices[].delta {content, reasoning_content, tool_calls[]}, terminated by `data: [DONE]`. Usage is ALWAYS included in the final chunk (unlike OpenAI, no need for stream_options.include_usage, though it is accepted). stream_options sub-fields: include_usage (bool), include_internal_content (bool), buffer_tokens (int, coalesce N text deltas per SSE chunk), buffer_ms (number, coalesce up to N ms), buffer_mode "any"|"all" (when both buffers set). Streaming tool calls: arguments arrive incrementally; accumulate by tool_calls[i].index until finish_reason == "tool_calls". Reasoning streams in delta.reasoning_content alongside delta.content. Perf headers (fireworks-*) and rate-limit headers are only populated on NON-streaming responses; for streams set perf_metrics_in_response=true to get a perf_metrics object in the body.
tools_format: OpenAI shape: tools=[{"type":"function","function":{"name","description","parameters":{JSON Schema object with type/properties/required}}}]. Name: alphanumeric/underscore/dash, max 64 chars. Schema: JSON Schema 2020-12 types string/number/integer/object/array/boolean/null, enum, $defs, in-document $ref (#/...) only — external URI refs fail with "Error resolving schema reference". tool_choice: "auto" (default) | "none" | "required" | "any" (Fireworks alias for required, from the FireFunction era) | {"type":"function","function":{"name":"fn"}} or {"type":"function","name":"fn"} | {"type":"allowed_tools","allowed_tools":{"mode":"auto"|"required","tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"..."}}]}}. parallel_tool_calls: boolean (model-dependent). Tool result: {"role":"tool","tool_call_id":<id>,"content":<string>}. Response: choices[].message.tool_calls[] with finish_reason "tool_calls". Not all models support tools — check supportsTools on the model object; docs recommend temperature 0.0–0.3 for tool calling.
list_models_endpoint: GET https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1/models  (OpenAI-compatible; confirmed live — returns 401 without a key; OpenAI SDK client.models.list() works; there is NO dedicated docs page, so its exact extra fields are unverified: expect the standard {"object":"list","data":[{"id","object":"model","created","owned_by"}]} with third-party-reported extras context_length, supports_image_input, supports_tools). Richer, documented control-plane catalogue: GET https://api.fireworks.ai/v1/accounts/fireworks/models?pageSize=200[&pageToken=..][&filter=<AIP-160 grammar>][&readMask=*] — returns {"models":[gatewayModel...],"nextPageToken","totalSize"}; per LiteLLM issue #26537, filter on supports_serverless=true to get the public serverless catalogue (filter key casing not officially confirmed; response uses camelCase supportsServerless). GET /v1/accounts/{your_account}/models lists only your own models/deployments.
model_fields: Model ID format: "accounts/fireworks/models/<slug>" where slugs encode dots as "p" (deepseek-v3p1, kimi-k2p6, glm-5p2, qwen3-8b); Fast-tier IDs are routers "accounts/fireworks/routers/<slug>-turbo" or "<slug>-fast"; dedicated deployments "accounts/<account>/deployments/<id>". Control-plane gatewayModel fields (GET /v1/accounts/{account}/models): name (resource path), displayName (<64 chars), description (<1000), state (UPLOADING|READY), createTime, updateTime, kind (HF_BASE_MODEL | HF_PEFT_ADDON | EMBEDDING_MODEL | ...), contextLength, supportsTools, supportsImageInput, supportsLora, supportsFireattention, supportsServerless, serverlessModes[], conversationConfig (chat template), defaultSamplingParams, baseModelDetails/peftDetails/teftDetails, deployedModelRefs[]. OpenAI-style /inference/v1/models: id, object="model", created, owned_by (+ unverified context_length, supports_image_input, supports_tools). No pricing fields on either model object.
pricing_source: No pricing API and no cost field in responses; pricing must be a hand-maintained table. Human sources: https://docs.fireworks.ai/serverless/pricing (per-1M input / cached-input / output, Standard vs Priority columns) and the model library https://fireworks.ai/models ("$X/M Input • $Y/M Output • context"). Community machine-readable: models.dev, provider dir providers/fireworks-ai/models/accounts/fireworks/{models,routers}/*.toml with cost.input/cost.output/cost.cache_read and limit.context/limit.output. Headline rates (USD per 1M, Standard, input/cached/output): Kimi K3 $3.00/$0.30/$15.00 (Priority $3.75/$0.375/$18.75); DeepSeek V4.1 Flash $0.30/$0.006/$1.20 (library page shows $0.22/$0.66 — pages disagree); GLM 5.3 Flash $0.15/$0.03/$0.50; Qwen 3.8 Max $2.00/$0.25/$6.00; Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B $0.05/$0.01/$0.20; DeepSeek V4 Pro $1.74/$0.145/$3.48. Fallback parameter buckets for unlisted models (same rate input and output): <4B $0.10, 4B–16B $0.20, >16B $0.90. Multipliers: Priority (service_tier="priority") ~1.5x; Batch API 50%; US-only models 1.5x from 2026-09-01 (GLM 5.2 Fast US exempt). Cached input: pricing table lists ~10% of input rate, while the prompt-caching guide says "default 50% discount, varies by model" — treat as model-specific. Embeddings $0.008–$0.10/1M. $1 free credit on signup.
quirks: Model IDs are full resource paths (accounts/fireworks/models/<slug>); dots in versions become 'p' (deepseek-v3p1, kimi-k2p6). Fast tier uses different router IDs (accounts/fireworks/routers/<slug>-turbo); Priority tier is a request param service_tier:"priority" (~1.5x price, only 'priority' accepted); US-only models live on us.api.fireworks.ai at 1.5x.

max_tokens defaults to 2048 — too low for agentic/coding turns, always set it. max_completion_tokens is accepted as an alias (mutually exclusive with max_tokens). If prompt+max_tokens exceeds context, Fireworks silently SHRINKS max_tokens instead of erroring (context_length_exceeded_behavior default "truncate"; set "error" for OpenAI-like failure). prompt_truncate_len evicts oldest messages but preserves the system prompt.
System prompt goes in messages as the first role:"system" message (standard). Setting its content to an empty string suppresses the model's built-in default system prompt.

tool_choice accepts OpenAI values plus "any" (alias of "required"), two function-object shapes ({type:function,function:{name}} and {type:function,name}), and an allowed_tools object {type:"allowed_tools",allowed_tools:{mode,tools}}. parallel_tool_calls is model-dependent; some serverless models have no tool support at all (check supportsTools). Docs advise temperature 0.0–0.3 for tool calls. Tool schemas: only in-document $ref; recursive $defs may fail on older deployment images.

Streaming always returns usage in the final chunk (OpenAI does not by default). Fireworks-only stream_options: buffer_tokens / buffer_ms / buffer_mode to coalesce SSE chunks, include_internal_content. Stream terminates with data: [DONE].

Perf headers (fireworks-prompt-tokens, fireworks-cached-prompt-tokens, fireworks-server-time-to-first-token) and rate-limit headers are only on non-streaming responses; for streams set perf_metrics_in_response=true to get perf_metrics in the body (prompt-tokens, cached-prompt-tokens, server-time-to-first-token, server-processing-time, speculation-*).

No cost/price in usage and no pricing API; official pricing pages disagree with each other (cached tokens 10% vs 50%; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash $0.30 vs $0.22 input). Keep a hand-maintained per-model table with the <4B/$0.10, 4–16B/$0.20, >16B/$0.90 parameter-bucket fallback, or sync from models.dev.

response_format shapes: {type:"text"} | {type:"json_object"} | {type:"json_schema",json_schema:{name,schema[,strict]}} | {type:"grammar",grammar:"<BNF>"}. Using json_schema on a reasoning model DISABLES reasoning output. You MUST tell the model to emit JSON in the prompt (else it can emit whitespace until max_tokens) and ideally include the schema in the prompt too. Schemas with properties are auto-treated as unevaluatedProperties:false (no hallucinated keys). Regex pattern is best-effort (lookarounds ignored). strict is accepted in the OpenAI shape but not documented — do not rely on it; json_object has no top-level schema key in current docs. Check finish_reason=="length" for truncated JSON.

Reasoning: reasoning_effort accepts low|medium|high|xhigh|max|none|adaptive or an integer/bool (model-specific); Anthropic-style thinking:{type:enabled|disabled|adaptive,budget_tokens>=1024} overrides reasoning_effort (cannot combine); reasoning_history disabled|interleaved|preserved controls multi-turn reasoning. Reasoning is returned as a separate message.reasoning_content / delta.reasoning_content field (not <think> tags) and must be echoed back in assistant messages to keep the chain; interleaved thinking between tool calls requires the last message role to be "tool". usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens reports reasoning spend.

Rate limits: 10 RPM account-wide with no payment method; hard fixed ceiling 6,000 RPM with payment method. Serverless TPM is adaptive by model size (<400B: 64.8M prompt / 16.2M uncached / 648k generated; 400B–1.6T: 43.2M/10.8M/432k; >=1.6T: 21.6M/5.4M/216k) and by spending tier (T1 $50, T2 $500, T3 $5k, T4 $50k monthly). 429 = adaptive limit exceeded; 503 = load shedding even within limits (Priority tier sheds last). No Retry-After header documented — use exponential backoff.

Prompt caching is automatic and prefix-based (exact token-prefix match); cached count in usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens and fireworks-cached-prompt-tokens header. Use prompt_cache_key body field or x-session-affinity header (or user field) for replica affinity; prompt_cache_isolation_key / x-prompt-cache-isolation-key to prevent cross-tenant sharing. Keep static content first and avoid timestamps in the system prompt.

Extra sampling knobs beyond OpenAI: top_k (0–100), min_p, typical_p, repetition_penalty (0–2), mirostat_target/mirostat_lr, seed, logit_bias by token id, n up to 128 (burns quota), logprobs as bool or int, return_token_ids, echo/echo_last, ignore_eos, raw_output, prompt_token_ids (bypasses chat template), speculation/prediction for speculative decoding, metadata object for tracing.

Vision: OpenAI image_url content parts (URLs or data:image/...;base64). Limits: max 30 images/request, base64 total <10MB, each URL <5MB, 1.5s download timeout; formats png/jpg/jpeg/gif/bmp/tiff/ppm; Llama 3.2 Vision wants images before text. Fireworks-specific '#transform=inline' URL fragment inlines documents/images for non-vision models (LiteLLM appends it automatically).

Also exposes an Anthropic-compatible POST /inference/v1/messages (Bearer auth, no anthropic-version header; use Anthropic SDK with base_url https://api.fireworks.ai/inference) and a beta OpenAI Responses API POST /inference/v1/responses with server-side agent loop and MCP tools ({type:"sse",server_url}).

Model listing: the OpenAI-style GET /inference/v1/models exists but is undocumented; the documented control-plane list is per-account and paginated (pageSize<=200, pageToken, AIP-160 filter); use account 'fireworks' with a supports_serverless filter to get the public serverless catalogue rather than your own (usually empty) account. Fireworks' own Python SDK is alpha — the OpenAI SDK with base_url is the recommended client. Every response carries x-request-id / request_id for support.
rate_limit_headers: Officially documented (non-streaming responses only, values in tokens-per-minute): X-Ratelimit-Limit-Tokens-Prompt (total prompt TPM, cached+uncached), X-Ratelimit-Limit-Tokens-Cache-Adjusted-Prompt (uncached/cache-adjusted prompt TPM), X-Ratelimit-Limit-Tokens-Generated (output TPM). Third-party pages additionally report x-ratelimit-limit-requests, x-ratelimit-remaining-requests, x-ratelimit-reset-requests and x-ratelimit-over-limit: yes — NOT present in official docs, treat as unverified/optional. No Retry-After documented. Also present: x-request-id; perf headers fireworks-prompt-tokens, fireworks-cached-prompt-tokens, fireworks-server-time-to-first-token. Status codes: 429 = adaptive rate limit exceeded (or GPU saturation on dedicated deployments), 503 = load shedding; recommended handling is exponential backoff, or service_tier="priority" to shed last.
reasoning_params: reasoning_effort: "low" | "medium" | "high" | "xhigh" | "max" | "none" | "adaptive" | integer (token budget) | bool — support is model-specific (DeepSeek R1/V3.1+, Qwen3, Kimi K2.x/K3, GLM 4.7/5.x, MiniMax-M2, GPT-OSS). thinking: {"type":"enabled"|"disabled"|"adaptive","budget_tokens":>=1024} (Anthropic-compatible; overrides reasoning_effort; not combinable). reasoning_history: "disabled" | "interleaved" | "preserved" (how prior reasoning is rendered into multi-turn prompts). Output: choices[].message.reasoning_content (non-streaming) and choices[].delta.reasoning_content (streaming); usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens (also mirrored as output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens). Pass reasoning_content back inside assistant messages to preserve the chain; interleaved thinking between tool calls requires the last message to be role "tool". response_format json_schema disables reasoning output.
structured_output: response_format: {"type":"json_object"} (any valid JSON) | {"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":"<name>","schema":{...}[,"strict":true]}} (recommended; OpenAI strict shape accepted natively but strict not documented) | {"type":"grammar","grammar":"<BNF string>"} | {"type":"text"}. Supports most JSON Schema 2020-12: all primitive types, properties/required/additionalProperties, enum, $defs (and Draft-7 definitions), in-document $ref only (no external URIs), bare #/$defs/Foo shorthand via lifting nested $defs to root. Schemas with properties are automatically enforced as unevaluatedProperties:false; pattern is best-effort. Quirks: must instruct the model to produce JSON in the prompt (else it may emit whitespace until max_tokens) and docs recommend including the schema in the prompt as well; check finish_reason=="length" for truncated JSON; json_schema disables reasoning on reasoning models; some models can emit reasoning_content alongside JSON. OpenAI SDK client.chat.completions.parse works via the standard json_schema shape.
usage_and_cost_in_response: usage is on every response (non-streaming body and the final streaming chunk): {"prompt_tokens","completion_tokens","total_tokens","prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens"},"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens"},"output_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens"}}. There is NO cost/price field anywhere in the response — compute cost client-side as (prompt_tokens - cached_tokens)*input + cached_tokens*cached_rate + completion_tokens*output from a maintained price table (Priority x1.5, batch x0.5, US x1.5). Optional perf_metrics body object when perf_metrics_in_response=true (prompt-tokens, cached-prompt-tokens, server-time-to-first-token, server-processing-time seconds, speculation-* stats; deployment-only backend-host/num-concurrent-requests/queue/prefill/generation durations); same metrics are in fireworks-* headers for non-streaming calls.

provider: Google Gemini API (Google AI for Developers, generativelanguage.googleapis.com) — classic generateContent surface, now labelled "Gemini Generate Content API (Legacy)" in docs but "fully supported"; the newer stateful Interactions API (client.interactions.create, GA June 2026) is what the top-level guides now document.
base_url: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta (stable channel: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1 — SDKs default to v1beta; select with httpOptions.apiVersion). OpenAI-compatible shim: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/
auth_header: x-goog-api-key: <API_KEY> (REST reference examples also accept ?key=<API_KEY> as a query parameter, e.g. ...:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse&key=...). SDK env-var precedence: GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY; "If both are set, GOOGLE_API_KEY takes precedence." The OpenAI-compat layer instead uses Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>.
chat_endpoint: POST https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent  (path form {model=models/*}). Request body (camelCase or snake_case both accepted in REST): {"contents":[{"role":"user"|"model","parts":[{"text":...}|{"inlineData":{mimeType,data}}|{"fileData":...}|{"functionCall":...}|{"functionResponse":...}]}], "systemInstruction":{"parts":[{"text":...}]}, "tools":[...], "toolConfig":{...}, "generationConfig":{"maxOutputTokens","temperature"(0-2),"topP","topK","stopSequences"[],"candidateCount","seed","presencePenalty","frequencyPenalty","responseMimeType","responseSchema","responseJsonSchema","responseFormat","responseModalities","mediaResolution","responseLogprobs","logprobs","speechConfig","imageConfig","enableEnhancedCivicAnswers","thinkingConfig"}, "safetySettings":[...], "cachedContent":"cachedContents/{id}", "serviceTier":"standard"|"flex"|"priority"}. Response: {"candidates":[{"content":{"role":"model","parts":[...]},"finishReason","safetyRatings","citationMetadata","groundingMetadata","urlContextMetadata","avgLogprobs","logprobsResult","tokenCount","index","finishMessage"}],"promptFeedback":{"blockReason"},"usageMetadata":{...},"modelVersion","responseId"}. finishReason enum: FINISH_REASON_UNSPECIFIED, STOP, MAX_TOKENS, SAFETY, RECITATION, LANGUAGE, OTHER, BLOCKLIST, PROHIBITED_CONTENT, SPII, MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL, IMAGE_SAFETY, IMAGE_PROHIBITED_CONTENT, IMAGE_RECITATION, IMAGE_OTHER, NO_IMAGE, UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL, TOO_MANY_TOOL_CALLS. Token pre-count: POST /v1beta/models/{model}:countTokens ({"contents":[...]} or {"generateContentRequest":{...}}) -> {"totalTokens", "cachedContentTokenCount"}.
streaming: POST https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse — Server-Sent Events; each "data: {...}" line is a full GenerateContentResponse chunk (candidates[].content.parts[] deltas; concatenate parts[].text). WITHOUT ?alt=sse the server streams a JSON array of GenerateContentResponse objects instead (harder to parse incrementally) — always add alt=sse. usageMetadata appears on multiple chunks, not only the last; the final chunk carries the complete counts and finishReason. Structured-output streams are "valid partial JSON strings, which can be concatenated to form the final, complete JSON object." With thinking on, a Gemini 3 text response may deliver its thoughtSignature "in a part with an empty text content part" — do not drop empty-text parts that carry a signature. No [DONE] sentinel; the stream just ends.
tools_format: Declared as "tools":[{"functionDeclarations":[{"name","description","parameters":{OpenAPI-3.0.3-subset Schema: type STRING|NUMBER|INTEGER|BOOLEAN|ARRAY|OBJECT|NULL, properties, required, enum, items, nullable, format, description, minimum/maximum, minItems/maxItems, anyOf, propertyOrdering...} OR "parametersJsonSchema":{standard JSON Schema}, optional "response"/"responseJsonSchema", "behavior"}]}] — one Tool object holds MANY functionDeclarations (not one tool per function). Built-in tools are sibling Tool objects: {"googleSearch":{}}, {"codeExecution":{}}, {"urlContext":{}}, {"fileSearch":...}, {"computerUse":...}. Function name rule: "Must be a-z, A-Z, 0-9, or contain underscores and dashes, with a maximum length of 128." Tool choice = "toolConfig":{"functionCallingConfig":{"mode":"AUTO"|"ANY"|"NONE"|"VALIDATED","allowedFunctionNames":["..."]}} — AUTO: default when only functionDeclarations present; ANY: always emits a function call with schema adherence (allowedFunctionNames restricts set); NONE: disables calls without removing declarations; VALIDATED: default when combining functions with built-in tools or structured output, constrained decoding for either a valid call or text. There is no OpenAI-style strict:true — ANY/VALIDATED provide schema adherence. Model output: parts[{"functionCall":{"id":"...","name":"...","args":{...}},"thoughtSignature":"<base64>"}] (parallel calls = several functionCall parts in one candidate; only the FIRST carries thoughtSignature; Gemini 3 "always returns a unique id"). Reply in a NEW Content with "role":"user" (only 'user'/'model' roles are valid): parts[{"functionResponse":{"id":"<same id>","name":"...","response":{...JSON object — any keys, e.g. "output"/"result"; use "error" key for failures}}}]; response must be an object, so wrap scalars/arrays. Gemini 3 also accepts multimodal functionResponse.parts (inlineData image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, application/pdf, text/plain). Echo the model's functionCall parts verbatim (including thoughtSignature and id) into history before the functionResponse turn.
list_models_endpoint: GET https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models?pageSize=<=1000&pageToken=... (default pageSize 50) -> {"models":[Model...],"nextPageToken"}; single model: GET /v1beta/models/{model}. OpenAI-compat: GET /v1beta/openai/models and /v1beta/openai/models/{model}.
model_fields: Model resource: name ("models/{model}"), baseModelId ("pass this to the generation request"), version, displayName (<=128 UTF-8 chars), description, inputTokenLimit (int), outputTokenLimit (int), supportedGenerationMethods[] (strings such as generateContent, streamGenerateContent, countTokens, createCachedContent, batchGenerateContent — filter on this to hide embedding/TTS/image models), thinking (bool — "Whether the model supports thinking"), temperature, maxTemperature, topP, topK. No pricing, no capability flags for function-calling/structured-output, no knowledge cutoff, no deprecation date in the API — those live only on docs pages. Current text models (per-model docs pages, all 1,048,576 in / 65,536 out): gemini-3.8-flash (GA Sep 2026; thinking low/medium/high), gemini-3.7-flash, gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.5-flash, gemini-3.5-flash-lite, gemini-3.1-flash-lite, gemini-3.1-pro-preview, gemini-3-flash-preview, gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.5-flash-lite (2.5 family knowledge cutoff Jan 2025). Aliases: gemini-flash-latest / gemini-flash-lite-latest / gemini-pro-latest hot-swap with 2-week email notice. Naming: stable (gemini-3.6-flash), preview (gemini-2.5-flash-preview-09-2025, 2-week deprecation notice), latest, experimental.
pricing_source: Docs page only — https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing ; no pricing endpoint and no cost in responses. Paid tier, USD per 1M tokens (output prices include thinking tokens): gemini-3.8-flash / 3.7-flash / 3.6-flash: in $0.75, out $3.75 through 2026-12-31 (then $1.50 / $7.50 from 2027-01-01), cache read $0.075, storage $0.50/M-tok/hr; gemini-3.5-flash: $1.50 / $9.00, cache $0.15; gemini-3.5-flash-lite: $0.30 / $2.50, cache $0.03; gemini-3.1-pro-preview: $2.00 in (text/image), $12.00 out (text+thinking), $120 image-out — the Gemini 3 guide notes a >200k-token tier of $4/$18; gemini-3-flash-preview: $0.50 in ($1.00 audio), $3.00 out, cache $0.05; gemini-2.5-pro: $1.25 in / $10.00 out for prompts <=200k tokens, $2.50 / $15.00 for >200k, cache $0.125/$0.25, storage $4.50/hr; gemini-2.5-flash: $0.30 in ($1.00 audio), $2.50 out, cache $0.03; gemini-2.5-flash-lite: $0.10 in ($0.30 audio), $0.40 out, cache $0.01. Batch API = 50% off everything. Grounding with Google Search: Gemini 3.x 5,000 free requests/month shared then $14/1,000; Gemini 2.5 1,500 RPD free then $35/1,000 grounded prompts. Free tier exists (content may be used to improve products). Cache storage billed per M tokens per hour.
quirks: Docs split: every guide under /gemini-api/docs/<topic> now shows the Interactions API (snake_case steps/response_format/tool_choice/thinking_level, previous_interaction_id). The generateContent wire format lives under /gemini-api/docs/generate-content/<topic> and /api/generate-content and is labelled 'Legacy' though 'fully supported'. Do not mix the two shapes.

System prompt: top-level request field systemInstruction (snake: system_instruction), a Content object {"parts":[{"text":...}]}; role is ignored; text-only ('Only text should be used in parts and content in each part will be in a separate paragraph'). There is NO system role inside contents — contents roles must be exactly 'user' or 'model' (400 otherwise).

max_tokens is generationConfig.maxOutputTokens. Thinking tokens are NOT capped by it separately but count as output for billing; usageMetadata.candidatesTokenCount excludes thoughts, thoughtsTokenCount holds them, totalTokenCount = prompt + thoughts + candidates.
Model path: 'models/gemini-3.8-flash' with RPC-style colon verbs (:generateContent, :streamGenerateContent, :countTokens). REST accepts camelCase or snake_case field names interchangeably.

Thought signatures (Gemini 3, also 2.5 with thinking + function calling): Part.thoughtSignature (base64). For Gemini 3 function calling you MUST echo the signature on the first functionCall part of each step in the current turn or get 400 'Function call <name> in the <index> content block is missing a thought_signature'. Parallel calls: only the first functionCall part has one. Sequential multi-step loops: ALL signatures must be preserved. Text/final parts: signature on the last part, echoing is 'strictly recommended' not enforced. Dummy values 'context_engineering_is_the_way_to_go' or 'skip_thought_signature_validator' bypass the validator when injecting synthetic calls or importing history from another model. Streaming may send the signature in a part with empty text.
Gemini 3 always returns functionCall.id; send it back as functionResponse.id and match by id, not order.
functionResponse.response must be a JSON object (Struct); wrap scalar/array results, use an 'error' key for failures.

thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel (Gemini 3+) and thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget (2.5) are mutually exclusive in one request; thinkingLevel on a 2.5 model 'results in an error'. Thinking cannot be disabled on gemini-2.5-pro (min 128) or any Gemini 3 model (lowest is 'minimal'/'low'). Defaults: 3.1 Pro high, 3.x Flash medium, 3.x Flash-Lite minimal, 2.5 Pro/Flash dynamic(-1), 2.5 Flash-Lite off.

Gemini 3: 'strongly recommend keeping the temperature parameter at its default value of 1.0' — lower values can cause looping/degraded output. For 2.5 function calling the docs suggest temperature 0 for determinism.

Structured output: three overlapping mechanisms in generationConfig — (a) new responseFormat:{text:{mimeType:'APPLICATION_JSON', schema:{JSON Schema}}} (what the legacy guide now shows), (b) responseMimeType:'application/json' + responseJsonSchema (standard JSON Schema, Gemini 2.5+), (c) responseMimeType + responseSchema (OpenAPI-subset Schema object with propertyOrdering; type values are UPPERCASE enums). Also responseMimeType 'text/x.enum' for enum-only output. Combining structured output with tools/function calling is Gemini 3 only (preview); on 2.5 it is not supported. Unsupported schema keywords are silently ignored; very large/deeply nested schemas are rejected; schema tokens count as input.

Structured-output/function schema subset: type (incl. null), title, description, properties, required, additionalProperties, enum, format (date-time/date/time), minimum/maximum, items, prefixItems, minItems/maxItems, anyOf, $ref ('#' recursion). No oneOf/allOf/patternProperties/if-then.
Streaming without ?alt=sse returns a JSON array, not SSE. With alt=sse there is no [DONE] sentinel.

Rate limits: measured RPM / TPM (input tokens) / RPD (reset midnight Pacific), applied per project not per key, plus spend caps on a rolling 10-minute window (Tier1 $10, Tier2 $50, Tier3 $200). Exceeding any returns HTTP 429 with google.rpc status RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. The rate-limits page no longer publishes per-model RPM/TPM/RPD tables — 'View your active rate limits in AI Studio'. Priority tier limits default to 0.3x standard. No rate-limit or Retry-After headers are documented; SDKs retry 429/5xx/408 with exponential backoff (Python: 4 retries, ~1s initial, 60s max).

Error body is the standard Google API shape {"error":{"code":<http>,"message","status":"RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED|INVALID_ARGUMENT|FAILED_PRECONDITION|PERMISSION_DENIED|NOT_FOUND|INTERNAL|UNAVAILABLE|DEADLINE_EXCEEDED","details":[...]}}; 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION is typically 'free tier not available in your country / enable billing'; 402 = depleted prepay credits. Prompt-level blocks arrive as HTTP 200 with promptFeedback.blockReason (SAFETY|OTHER|BLOCKLIST|PROHIBITED_CONTENT|IMAGE_SAFETY) and empty candidates — check before indexing candidates[0].

Caching: implicit caching is on by default for 2.5+ (min 2,048 tokens for 2.5, 4,096 for Gemini 3.x); hits show up as usageMetadata.cachedContentTokenCount and are auto-discounted (put stable content first). Explicit caching = POST /v1beta/cachedContents then generationConfig-level 'cachedContent':'cachedContents/{id}'; explicit cache model must match exactly.
GOOGLE_API_KEY overrides GEMINI_API_KEY in the official SDKs — surprising when both are set.

OpenAI-compat shim (/v1beta/openai/, Authorization: Bearer): chat/completions, embeddings, models, images/generations, videos, batches; reasoning_effort maps minimal/low/medium/high -> thinking_level on Gemini 3 and 1,024/1,024/8,192/24,576 thinking_budget on 2.5; reasoning_effort 'none' only for 2.5 Flash/Flash-Lite; use extra_body.google.thinking_config {thinking_level|thinking_budget, include_thoughts} instead (cannot combine with reasoning_effort). Unlisted parameters are 'silently ignored'. Still beta.

Deprecations to avoid in pickers: gemini-3-pro-preview (shut down 2026-03-09 -> gemini-3.1-pro-preview), gemini-2.0-flash/-lite (shut down 2026-06-01), gemini-2.5-*-preview-* dated snapshots (shut down Nov 2025-Mar 2026), gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview (2026-05-25). gemini-3-flash-preview still live with no shutdown date.
Free-tier note: free-tier traffic 'content used to improve our products'; paid tier is not. Preview/experimental models have tighter limits.

usageMetadata has no cost field; compute cost client-side from the pricing page, applying the >200k-token prompt tier for gemini-2.5-pro / gemini-3.1-pro-preview and the date-based price step for 3.8/3.7/3.6 Flash on 2027-01-01.
rate_limit_headers: None documented. The official rate-limits, troubleshooting and api-errors pages mention no x-ratelimit-*, x-goog-quota-* or Retry-After response headers; limits are only visible in AI Studio and via 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED errors (body error.status = "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED"; treat 429/503/408/5xx as retryable with exponential backoff + jitter; do not retry 400/402/403). Rate limits are per project (not per key) across RPM, TPM (input), RPD and a rolling 10-minute spend cap by tier.
reasoning_params: generationConfig.thinkingConfig = {"includeThoughts": bool, "thinkingBudget": int, "thinkingLevel": enum}. thinkingLevel (Gemini 3+; error on 2.5): enum THINKING_LEVEL_UNSPECIFIED | MINIMAL | LOW | MEDIUM | HIGH — REST examples use lowercase strings ("thinkingLevel":"low"). Support: gemini-3.8/3.7-flash low/medium(default)/high; gemini-3.6/3.5-flash minimal/low/medium(default)/high; gemini-3.1-pro-preview low/medium/high(default, no minimal); gemini-3.5/3.1-flash-lite minimal(default)/low/medium/high. Cannot fully disable on any Gemini 3 model. thinkingBudget (Gemini 2.5): gemini-2.5-pro 128–32768 (default dynamic, cannot disable), gemini-2.5-flash 0–24576 (0 disables), gemini-2.5-flash-lite 512–24576 (default off, 0 disables); -1 = dynamic; still accepted on Gemini 3 for backward compatibility but "You cannot use both thinking_level and the legacy thinking_budget parameter in the same request." includeThoughts:true returns summary parts with "thought": true (may be absent/empty — always handle). Thought signatures come back on parts as "thoughtSignature" (base64) and must be echoed (see quirks). usageMetadata.thoughtsTokenCount reports thinking tokens; billed at output price. Recommended: leave temperature at 1.0 on Gemini 3.
structured_output: Three co-existing forms inside generationConfig: (1) newest: "responseFormat":{"text":{"mimeType":"APPLICATION_JSON","schema":{<JSON Schema>}}} (ResponseFormatConfig/TextResponseFormat; what the legacy structured-output guide now shows; schema "Only applicable when mimeType is APPLICATION_JSON"); (2) "responseMimeType":"application/json" + "responseJsonSchema":{<standard JSON Schema, Gemini 2.5+>} — recommended over (3); (3) "responseMimeType":"application/json" + "responseSchema":{OpenAPI-subset Schema object: "type":"OBJECT"/"ARRAY"/"STRING"/"NUMBER"/"INTEGER"/"BOOLEAN"/"NULL", properties, required, enum, items, nullable, format, minimum/maximum, minItems/maxItems, anyOf, "propertyOrdering":[...] to fix key order}. Enum-only output: "responseMimeType":"text/x.enum" with a string enum schema. Supported JSON Schema keywords: types incl. null, title, description, properties, required, additionalProperties, enum, format (date-time/date/time), minimum/maximum, items, prefixItems, minItems/maxItems, anyOf, $ref (recursive "#"). Unsupported keywords are ignored; huge/deep schemas rejected; schema tokens count as input. Streaming yields concatenable partial JSON. Combining structured output with tools (Google Search, URL Context, Code Execution, File Search, Function Calling) is Gemini 3-only (preview); not on 2.5. No 'strict' flag; constrained decoding is implied.
usage_and_cost_in_response: usageMetadata (on non-stream response and on stream chunks; final chunk complete): promptTokenCount (input, includes cached tokens), cachedContentTokenCount (portion served from cache), candidatesTokenCount (visible output across candidates, excludes thoughts), thoughtsTokenCount (reasoning tokens, billed as output), toolUsePromptTokenCount (tokens in tool-use prompts, e.g. grounding), totalTokenCount (prompt + thoughts + candidates), plus per-modality breakdowns promptTokensDetails[], cacheTokensDetails[], candidatesTokensDetails[], toolUsePromptTokensDetails[] each {modality: TEXT|IMAGE|AUDIO|VIDEO|DOCUMENT, tokenCount}. Also modelVersion (exact served version, useful for -latest aliases) and responseId. NO cost/price field anywhere; compute cost = promptTokenCount−cachedContentTokenCount at input price + cachedContentTokenCount at cache price + (candidatesTokenCount + thoughtsTokenCount) at output price, using the >200k-prompt tier where applicable. Pre-flight sizing via POST models/{model}:countTokens -> {totalTokens}.

provider: xAI (Grok API) — OpenAI-compatible REST API; env var convention XAI_API_KEY
base_url: https://api.x.ai/v1 (global; routes across regions). US data-residency variant: https://us.api.x.ai/v1 (only grok-4.7 and grok-4.6; other model IDs 404 there; token prices +10%). Management API (separate key, not needed for inference): https://management-api.x.ai. With the OpenAI SDK the base_url MUST include the trailing /v1 or every call 404s.
auth_header: Authorization: Bearer $XAI_API_KEY (same header for all inference endpoints; 401 = missing/invalid, 403 = insufficient permissions/ACL)
chat_endpoint: POST /v1/chat/completions (OpenAI-compatible; officially labelled "legacy" — still fully supported, but new features land first on POST /v1/responses). Async variant: same endpoint with "deferred": true returns {request_id}; poll GET /v1/chat/deferred-completion/{request_id} (202 while processing, 200 with the normal completion body once ready; result retrievable once within 24h). Also available: POST /v1/responses (preferred; input/max_output_tokens/reasoning.effort/instructions/previous_response_id/store/include, server-side tools), POST /v1/tokenize-text (model, text -> token_ids[]), GET /v1/api-key (key metadata/ACLs). Anthropic-style POST /v1/messages and POST /v1/completions, /v1/complete exist but are "fully deprecated". No embeddings endpoint.
streaming: Set "stream": true. Server-Sent Events, each line `data: {json}` with object "chat.completion.chunk"; choices[].delta.{role, content, reasoning_content, tool_calls}; finish_reason null until the last content chunk ("stop" | "length" | "end_turn"); terminated by `data: [DONE]`. Usage (including usage.cost_in_usd_ticks and reasoning_tokens) is only emitted in a final extra chunk with empty choices when you send "stream_options": {"include_usage": true} — omit it and you get no usage. Tool calls are NOT streamed incrementally: a function call arrives whole in a single chunk. Reasoning models can be silent for a long time before the first delta — docs recommend raising client timeouts (examples use 3600 s). Streaming is unavailable on image-generation models. Citations/markdown links appear inline in delta.content as generated.
tools_format: OpenAI Chat Completions format: "tools": [{"type":"function","function":{"name","description","parameters":{JSON Schema, root must be type "object" (or oneOf/anyOf of objects); scalar/array roots are rejected}}}] — max 350 tools per request; "only functions are supported as a tool" on this endpoint. "tool_choice": "auto" (default) | "required" | "none" | {"type":"function","function":{"name":"..."}}. "parallel_tool_calls": true by default (false = at most one call). strict schema adherence is implicitly ALWAYS on for tool arguments (no strict flag needed). Response: choices[].message.tool_calls[] = {id, type:"function", function:{name, arguments: JSON-encoded string}}; reply with {role:"tool", tool_call_id, content}. Server-side tools ({"type":"web_search"}, "x_search", "code_interpreter", "collections_search", "image_generation", "mcp"; $5 per 1k calls) are documented only for /v1/responses; on chat completions use the legacy "search_parameters" object instead (see quirks).
list_models_endpoint: GET /v1/models (OpenAI-shaped minimal list; also GET /v1/models/{id}) and GET /v1/language-models (full detail for chat/vision models, wrapper {"models":[...]}; also GET /v1/language-models/{id}). Use /v1/language-models for pricing, aliases, modalities and per-model reasoning_effort capabilities. Separate GET /v1/image-generation-models and /v1/video-generation-models.
model_fields: GET /v1/language-models item: id (string), aliases (string[] — e.g. grok-4.3 -> ["grok-4.3-latest"], grok-build-0.1 -> ["grok-code-fast-1","grok-code-fast","grok-code-fast-1-0825"]; grok-4.7/4.6 list none), version (string), fingerprint (string), created (unix int), object ("model"), owned_by, context_length (int tokens; 500000 for grok-4.7/4.6/4.5, 1000000 for grok-4.3/4.20 variants, 256000 for grok-build-0.1), input_modalities (["text","image"]), output_modalities (["text"]), capabilities.reasoning_effort (string[] of accepted values, e.g. ["low","medium","high","xhigh"]) and capabilities.default_reasoning_effort (string|null), prompt_text_token_price, cached_prompt_text_token_price, prompt_image_token_price, completion_text_token_price, prompt_text_token_price_long_context, cached_prompt_text_token_price_long_context, completion_text_token_price_long_context (all integers in USD CENTS PER 100 MILLION TOKENS -> $/1M tokens = value / 10,000; 0 = feature unavailable or standard price applies), long_context_threshold (int tokens, currently 200000), search_price (USD cents per 100M searches). GET /v1/models returns the same core/pricing fields minus version/fingerprint/modalities/search_price.
pricing_source: Live: GET /v1/language-models (per-model prices as integer USD cents per 100M tokens, incl. cached and long-context tiers + long_context_threshold) and, per request, usage.cost_in_usd_ticks (1 USD = 10,000,000,000 ticks; the exact billed amount after cache discounts, incl. server-side tool charges and priority/regional multipliers). Static: https://docs.x.ai/developers/pricing (Sept 2026 text models, $/1M tokens input/cached/output, second value when prompt >= 200k tokens): grok-4.7 & grok-4.6 2.00/0.50/6.00 (4.00/1.00/12.00); grok-4.5 2.00/0.30/6.00 (4.00/0.60/12.00); grok-4.3, grok-4.20-0309-reasoning, grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning, grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309 1.25/0.20/2.50 (2.50/0.40/5.00); grok-build-0.1 1.00/0.20/2.00 (2.00/0.40/4.00). Reasoning tokens billed at output rate. Tools: web_search/x_search/code_execution $5 per 1k calls (x_search moving to $5/1k posts + $10/1k profiles from 2026-09-21), collections_search $2.50/1k, file attachments $10/1k. Multipliers: service_tier "priority" 2x tokens; us.api.x.ai 1.1x; Batch API -20% (grok-4.3 family only; not supported on 4.7/4.6/grok-build).
quirks: Base URL must be https://api.x.ai/v1 (with /v1) when using the OpenAI SDK; the SDK also defaults to OPENAI_API_KEY, so pass api_key explicitly from XAI_API_KEY.

Chat Completions is officially 'legacy': fully functional but server-side tools, encrypted reasoning, previous_response_id/store, response compaction and inline citation annotations exist only on POST /v1/responses; no shutdown date published. The Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages and /v1/completions are 'fully deprecated'.

Token cap: max_tokens is DEPRECATED in favour of max_completion_tokens (both still accepted); default is 128,000. Reasoning tokens count against it, so a small cap on a reasoning model yields empty content with finish_reason 'length'.

reasoning_effort is a flat top-level string and its accepted set differs per model — read capabilities.reasoning_effort / default_reasoning_effort from /v1/language-models instead of hardcoding: grok-4.7 & grok-4.6 low|medium|high|xhigh (default high); grok-4.5 low|medium|high (rejects 'none'; 'xhigh' silently treated as 'high'); grok-4.3 none|low|medium|high|xhigh (default low; 'none' disables reasoning); grok-4.20-multi-agent uses effort to choose agent count. Reasoning cannot be turned off on grok-4.5+. The retired grok-4 (0709) returned an error for any reasoning_effort.

Reasoning models reject presence_penalty, frequency_penalty and stop with an error (strip them, do not send null). logit_bias is unsupported everywhere; logprobs/top_logprobs unsupported on grok-4.20 and newer; presence_penalty also unsupported on grok-3.

Chat Completions returns NO readable chain-of-thought for Grok 4.x: choices[].message.reasoning_content exists in the schema but is null/absent (docs: 'No reasoning content returned'); only usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens is exposed. /v1/responses returns reasoning.encrypted_content instead. When a prior assistant turn did include reasoning_content, echo it back verbatim — omitting it is 'the top cause of cache misses'.

System prompt placement: standard OpenAI {role:'system'} as the first message; the role enum also accepts 'developer' (and legacy 'function'). On /v1/responses use the 'instructions' field or a system input item.

finish_reason can be 'end_turn' (non-OpenAI value) in addition to 'stop' and 'length'; message.refusal may be set; top-level response may include citations[], service_tier, output_files[], system_fingerprint.

Structured outputs: response_format {type:'json_schema', json_schema:{name, schema, strict:true}} is guaranteed to match; {type:'json_object'} is lenient. additionalProperties defaults to FALSE (set true explicitly to allow extras); fields not in 'required' are optional; empty enum/anyOf -> HTTP 400; anyOf and oneOf behave identically; $ref/$defs must be non-circular; minLength/maxLength enforced up to 2048, min/maxItems up to 256, min/maxProperties up to 64; pattern is an ECMAScript subset (no backreferences, lookaround, word boundaries, Unicode property escapes); not / if-then-else / multi-allOf are best-effort only. Draft 2020-12 preferred, Draft-07 accepted. Tool-call argument schemas are implicitly strict.
Tools: max 350 functions per request; parameters root must be an object (or oneOf/anyOf of objects); streamed tool calls arrive whole in one chunk; parallel_tool_calls defaults true.

Long-context pricing: once the prompt reaches long_context_threshold (200k tokens) input, cached and output prices double for that request (also applies to grok-4.3/4.20 despite their 1M context). Pull the *_long_context fields and threshold from /v1/language-models.
Model-list prices are integers in USD cents per 100 MILLION tokens: $/1M tokens = value / 10,000 (e.g. 20000 -> $2.00/M). A 0 means unavailable (or standard price applies, for long-context fields).

usage.cost_in_usd_ticks is the exact billed amount (1 USD = 1e10 ticks) on every chat/responses/image/video reply; in streaming it only appears in the final usage chunk and only if stream_options.include_usage=true. Also usage.num_sources_used (live search) and usage.server_side_tool_usage_details (per-tool counts; only successful tool executions are billed).

Prompt caching is automatic (no cache_control markers), exact-prefix based on messages from the start, per-server: send header x-grok-conv-id (chat completions) or body prompt_cache_key (Responses; also listed in the chat-completions schema) with a stable conversation id for sticky routing. Editing, removing or reordering earlier messages breaks the cache; entries can be evicted under memory pressure. Cached tokens are included in prompt_tokens and STILL count toward TPM; cached price ~4-6x cheaper.

Rate limits are per model, tier-based (T0-T4 by cumulative spend since 2026-01-01: $0/$50/$250/$1k/$5k; tiers never downgrade), expressed as requests-per-SECOND plus tokens-per-minute (e.g. T0: grok-4.7 150 RPS/50M TPM; grok-4.3 & grok-build-0.1 37 RPS/10M TPM). 429 on excess; official docs document no rate-limit headers — treat x-ratelimit-* / Retry-After as optional and back off exponentially.

Live search on chat completions uses the legacy search_parameters object {mode:'off'|'on'|'auto', return_citations, from_date, to_date (YYYY-MM-DD), max_search_results, sources:[{type:'web'|'x'|'news'|'rss', ...}]} (web_search_options accepted as an OpenAI-compat shim); citations come back as a top-level citations[] of URLs and usage.num_sources_used. New server-side tools ({type:'web_search'} etc.) are Responses-only.
service_tier:'priority' opts into 2x-priced priority processing on chat completions/responses; you are billed at the priority rate only when the response's service_tier echoes 'priority'.

Regional: https://us.api.x.ai/v1 guarantees US processing but serves only grok-4.7/grok-4.6 (others 404), costs 10% more, and excludes Files/Collections/server-side tools; EU console availability lags (grok-4.5/4.6 restricted in EU at times).

Model IDs/aliases: -latest aliases exist for some models (grok-4.3-latest, grok-latest) but grok-4.7/4.6 have none — read aliases[] from /v1/language-models. Retired IDs (grok-4-0709, grok-4-fast-*, grok-4-1-fast-*, grok-code-fast-1) are server-side redirected since 2026-05-15 (non-reasoning slugs -> grok-4.3 with reasoning_effort 'none'; reasoning slugs -> grok-4.3; grok-code-fast* -> grok-build-0.1). Do not assume a listed alias has the same pricing row.

Deferred completions: deferred:true returns only {request_id}; poll GET /v1/chat/deferred-completion/{request_id} (202 = pending with empty body, 200 = done); the result can be fetched exactly once within 24h and shares the chat-completions rate limit.

Error handling: docs enumerate 400/401/403/404/405/415/422/429 but do not publish the error JSON shape — parse defensively (xAI historically returns a flat {code, error} object rather than OpenAI's nested {error:{message,type,code}}; unverified in this pass).

Image input: JPG/PNG only, <= 20 MiB per image, via image_url content parts with detail auto|low|high; token cost from prompt_image_token_price. No embeddings, speech or transcription endpoints on the upstream API.
Batch API (20% off) is only supported for the grok-4.3 / grok-4.20 family; grok-4.7, grok-4.6 and grok-build-0.1 pages say 'Batch API: not supported'.
rate_limit_headers: Not officially documented. https://docs.x.ai/developers/rate-limits documents only HTTP 429 plus per-model, per-tier RPS and TPM tables (tiers T0-T4 unlocked by cumulative spend $0/$50/$250/$1,000/$5,000 since 2026-01-01; Enterprise on request; tiers never downgrade; all prompt+completion+reasoning+cached tokens count toward TPM). Third-party integrators (OpenUsage, community guides) report OpenAI-style headers observed on responses: x-ratelimit-limit-requests, x-ratelimit-remaining-requests, x-ratelimit-reset-requests, x-ratelimit-limit-tokens, x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens, x-ratelimit-reset-tokens (format/units unspecified, parsed verbatim). Treat these and Retry-After as optional hints; implement exponential backoff on 429 regardless.
reasoning_params: Chat Completions: top-level "reasoning_effort": string (Responses API: "reasoning": {"effort": ...}). Accepted values per model, published in capabilities.reasoning_effort / default_reasoning_effort of /v1/language-models: grok-4.7 and grok-4.6 -> "low"|"medium"|"high"|"xhigh" (default "high"); grok-4.5 -> "low"|"medium"|"high" (default "high"; "xhigh" downgraded to "high"; "none" rejected); grok-4.3 -> "none"|"low"|"medium"|"high"|"xhigh" (default "low"; "none" = no reasoning); grok-4.20-0309-reasoning/-non-reasoning are fixed-mode variants; grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309 uses effort to pick agent count. Reasoning is mandatory on 4.5+ (effort only sets depth). Reasoning tokens are reported in usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens, billed at the output-token rate, count toward TPM and toward max_completion_tokens (default 128,000). Chat Completions does not return visible reasoning for Grok 4.x (message.reasoning_content null; Responses API offers include:["reasoning.encrypted_content"], returned automatically on grok-4.7). Reasoning models reject presence_penalty, frequency_penalty and stop; the retired grok-4 (0709) rejected reasoning_effort outright.
structured_output: response_format: {"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":"...","schema":{...},"strict":true}} for guaranteed schema-conformant JSON (strict is the intended mode; for tool arguments strict is implicitly always on); {"type":"json_object"} for lenient any-valid-JSON; {"type":"text"} default. Supported on the Grok 4 family (grok-4.7/4.6/4.5/4.3/4.20, grok-build-0.1 — each model page says "Structured outputs: Yes"). Schema support: string/number/integer/boolean/null, enum, const, array, object, anyOf/oneOf (identical semantics), non-circular $ref/$defs, string formats date/time/date-time/email/uuid/ipv4/ipv6/uri, numeric min/max/exclusive*, pattern (ECMAScript subset without backreferences/lookaround/word boundaries/Unicode property escapes); minLength/maxLength enforced to 2048, min/maxItems to 256, min/maxProperties to 64; best-effort only for not, if/then/else, multi-subschema allOf and other formats. Rules: additionalProperties defaults to false (explicitly set true to permit extras), non-required properties are optional, empty enum/anyOf -> 400, Draft 2020-12 works best (Draft-07 accepted). Works with OpenAI SDK helpers (zodResponseFormat, pydantic parse) and xAI SDK .parse().
usage_and_cost_in_response: usage: { prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, prompt_tokens_details: { cached_tokens, text_tokens, image_tokens, audio_tokens }, completion_tokens_details: { reasoning_tokens, audio_tokens, accepted_prediction_tokens, rejected_prediction_tokens }, num_sources_used (live-search sources), cost_in_usd_ticks (integer; 1 USD = 10,000,000,000 ticks; exact amount billed after cache discount, incl. server-side tool charges and priority/regional multipliers -> usd = ticks / 1e10), server_side_tool_usage_details: { code_interpreter, document_search, file_search, image_generation, mcp, web_search, x_search, x_posts_fetched, x_users_fetched } }. cached_tokens are a subset of prompt_tokens (bill them at cached price and the remainder at prompt price; long-context tier applies when prompt >= long_context_threshold). Top-level response also carries citations[] (URLs), service_tier ("default"|"priority"), system_fingerprint, output_files[]. In streaming, usage (and cost_in_usd_ticks) appears only in the final chunk with empty choices when stream_options.include_usage=true. Responses API mirrors this as usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens / output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens / cost_in_usd_ticks. Batch objects expose a cost_breakdown. GET /v1/api-key returns key metadata (redacted_api_key, api_key_id, user_id, team_id, acls, api_key_blocked, api_key_disabled, team_blocked, timestamps) — no balance fields in the current official schema.

provider: Meta. Two distinct products: (1) LEGACY "Llama API" public preview at api.llama.com — RETIRED 2026-07-06 (official notice page: llama.developer.meta.com/docs/llama-api-deprecation/, now redirects to ai.developer.meta.com and 404s; retirement confirmed by Promptfoo's provider page: "Meta retired the Llama API Public Preview on July 6, 2026, including api.llama.com"; requests now return a sunset response with redirect guidance). It served Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8, Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-FP8, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, Llama-3.3-8B-Instruct. (2) LIVE successor "Meta Model API" (dev.meta.ai, mirrored at ai.developer.meta.com) at api.meta.ai — serves Muse Spark 1.3/1.2/1.1 (+ -contributor tiers), muse-image-1.0, muse-voice-transcribe-1.0, sam-3.1. It serves NO Llama models; Meta directs Llama users to AWS Bedrock, Together, Groq, or self-hosting. A META_API_KEY that works today is a Meta Model API key (format `LLM|<numeric app id>|<secret>`). Recommendation for the harness: implement the "meta" provider against api.meta.ai/v1 (OpenAI-compatible), and treat api.llama.com only as a legacy alias that surfaces the sunset error.
base_url: LIVE (Meta Model API): https://api.meta.ai/v1 for OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Responses (point the OpenAI SDK base_url here). For the Anthropic SDK / Claude-style harnesses use host https://api.meta.ai (the SDK appends /v1/messages). Docs warn: no trailing slash. LEGACY (retired): native https://api.llama.com/v1 (SDK default; overridable via env LLAMA_API_CLIENT_BASE_URL) and OpenAI-compat https://api.llama.com/compat/v1/ — both return a sunset response since 2026-07-06.
auth_header: `Authorization: Bearer <key>` on every protocol, legacy and live. Live env var convention: MODEL_API_KEY (key looks like `LLM|607358788850350|nx9.....LJY`; shown once at creation in the "API keys" tab; keys on the same team share rate limits — limits are per team, not per key). The Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages surface ALSO uses Authorization: Bearer (not x-api-key) and does not require an anthropic-version header; for Claude Code set ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (not ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) plus ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.meta.ai. Legacy env var: LLAMA_API_KEY (same Bearer scheme).
chat_endpoint: LIVE: POST https://api.meta.ai/v1/chat/completions (OpenAI shape). Request: model (required, e.g. "muse-spark-1.3"), messages (roles user | assistant | developer | system | tool; system is treated identically to developer), temperature (0–2, default 1.0), top_p (>0, default 1.0), max_completion_tokens (output cap; shares the 1,048,576-token window with input; `max_tokens` is only a deprecated alias), stream, reasoning_effort (minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh), tools, tool_choice ("auto" only), parallel_tool_calls (default true), response_format, frequency_penalty (-2..2), presence_penalty (-2..2), seed (best-effort), safety_identifier (<=64 chars), prompt_cache_key, prompt_cache_retention ("in_memory" | "24h"). Response: {id:"chatcmpl-…", object:"chat.completion", created, model, choices:[{index, message:{role:"assistant", content, tool_calls?}, finish_reason:"stop"|"tool_calls"|"length"}], usage:{prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens}}. Rejected with HTTP 400: n>1, stop, logprobs:true, logit_bias, prediction, web_search_options, modalities, audio, text.format, reasoning_effort:"none". Errors use envelope {error:{message, type, code, param?}}. Alternatives on the same key: POST /v1/responses (recommended for agents: input, instructions, tools, reasoning.effort, previous_response_id, store (default true), include:["reasoning.encrypted_content"], max_output_tokens (min 16, includes reasoning), text.format, background) and POST /v1/messages (Anthropic shape: model, messages, max_tokens required, system, temperature 0–1, top_p, stream, thinking, output_config.effort/format, tools, tool_choice; POST /v1/messages/count_tokens also exists). LEGACY native: POST https://api.llama.com/v1/chat/completions with body {model, messages[{role:"user"|"system"|"tool"|"assistant", content: string | [{type:"text",text} | {type:"image_url",image_url:{url}}]}], tools, tool_choice, response_format, stream, max_completion_tokens, temperature, top_p, top_k, repetition_penalty, user}; response was NOT OpenAI-shaped: {id, completion_message:{role:"assistant", content: string | {type:"text",text}, stop_reason:"stop"|"tool_calls"|"length", tool_calls:[{id, function:{name, arguments: string}}]}, metrics:[{metric, value, unit}]}. Legacy compat: POST https://api.llama.com/compat/v1/chat/completions (OpenAI shape; also /compat/v1/moderations).
streaming: LIVE Chat Completions: stream:true → text/event-stream of OpenAI-style chunks (`data: {…choices:[{delta:{content | tool_calls[...]}, finish_reason}]}`), the final chunk carries finish_reason, terminated by `data: [DONE]`. Docs do not mention stream_options.include_usage or a usage object in the stream — treat usage-in-stream as unverified and fall back to non-streamed usage or client-side counting. LIVE Responses (/v1/responses, stream:true): named SSE events response.created, response.output_item.added / .done, response.output_text.delta / .done, response.function_call_arguments.delta / .done, response.reasoning_summary_text.delta / .done, response.completed / response.failed; background:true is incompatible with stream:true. LIVE Messages: Anthropic events message_start, content_block_start, content_block_delta, content_block_stop, message_delta, message_stop. LEGACY native: custom envelope per SSE chunk {id, event:{event_type:"start"|"progress"|"complete"|"metrics", delta:{type:"text", text} | {type:"tool_call", id?, function:{name?, arguments?}}, stop_reason?:"stop"|"tool_calls"|"length", metrics?:[{metric, value, unit}]}} — token counts arrive in a trailing "metrics" event; legacy compat streamed OpenAI chunks.
tools_format: LIVE Chat Completions: nested OpenAI format tools:[{type:"function", function:{name, description, parameters (JSON Schema; root type:"object" is added automatically if omitted), strict? (default false)}}]. Model returns choices[0].message.tool_calls:[{id, type:"function", function:{name, arguments: JSON string}}] with finish_reason "tool_calls"; results go back as {role:"tool", tool_call_id, content: string} and the full assistant message containing tool_calls must precede them. tool_choice: ONLY "auto" (the default) is accepted — "none", "required", and named {type:"function",function:{name}} all return HTTP 400 on both Chat Completions and Responses. parallel_tool_calls defaults true (set false to force one call per turn). Function names must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$ with AT MOST ONE dot (two or more dots → 400; use a namespace wrapper tool for nested names). call_id must be 1–64 chars. Arguments are "guided by your parameters schema but are not guaranteed to validate against it" unless strict:true (strict violations → 400). LIVE Responses API: flat tools [{type:"function", name, description, parameters, strict?}], output items function_call {call_id, name, arguments}, results as {type:"function_call_output", call_id, output}; custom freeform-text tools ({type:"custom", name, description}, no parameters) are Responses-only; built-in server tools {type:"web_search"} and {type:"tool_search"} (Responses/Messages only, not Chat Completions); max_tool_calls caps built-in tools only. LIVE Messages: Anthropic tool blocks; tool_choice auto | any | none | disable_parallel_tool_use; named tool choice → 400. LEGACY native: tools:[{type:"function", function:{name (<=64 chars, alphanumeric/underscore/dash), description?, parameters?, strict?}}]; tool_choice "none" | "auto" | "required" | {type:"function", function:{name}}; tool_calls on completion_message as [{id, function:{name, arguments: string — "the model does not always generate valid JSON"}}]; tool result {role:"tool", tool_call_id, content: string | [{type:"text",text}]}.
list_models_endpoint: LIVE: GET https://api.meta.ai/v1/models → {object:"list", data:[{id, object:"model", created, owned_by, metadata?}]}; GET https://api.meta.ai/v1/models/{model_id} for one model; also unauthenticated GET https://api.meta.ai/v1/status for health probing (good for a "is this key/base URL alive" check). Current IDs: muse-spark-1.3, muse-spark-1.2, muse-spark-1.1, muse-spark-1.3-contributor, muse-spark-1.2-contributor (chat/reasoning; 1,048,576-token context; text+image+video+PDF; audio full on 1.2, limited on 1.3), muse-image-1.0, muse-voice-transcribe-1.0, sam-3.1 (not chat models — filter by id prefix "muse-spark"). LEGACY native: GET https://api.llama.com/v1/models → bare JSON array (not {data:[…]}) of {id, object:"model", created, owned_by}; GET /v1/models/{model}. Legacy compat: GET https://api.llama.com/compat/v1/models and /compat/v1/models/{model} (OpenAI shape).
model_fields: LIVE model object: id (string), object ("model"), created (int, unix seconds), owned_by (string), metadata (optional object, keyed by client type, only present when a recognized `client` query parameter is sent). No context_length, modality, or pricing fields — the harness must hardcode capability metadata: muse-spark-* context 1,048,576 tokens, output cap 131,072 (per Meta's own OpenCode config example), input modalities text/image/pdf/video (audio on 1.2), reasoning:true. LEGACY model object: id, object ("model"), created, owned_by (no metadata); list response is a bare array.
