pricing_source: LIVE: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits (pay-as-you-go, USD per 1M tokens). Standard tier (muse-spark-1.3, -1.2, -1.1): input $1.25, cached input $0.15, output $4.25. Contributor tier (muse-spark-1.3-contributor, -1.2-contributor; Meta may train on prompts): input $0.10, cached input $0.002, output $0.20. Reasoning tokens bill at the output rate and count toward the output cap. Extras: web_search grounding $2.50 per 1,000 queries (billed separately, not in token usage), muse-image-1.0 $0.01 per generated image, muse-voice-transcribe-1.0 $0.18 per audio hour, sam-3.1 $2.50 per 1,000 images / $0.20 per 1,000 video frames. Prices are NOT returned by the API or the models endpoint — hardcode a table keyed by model id. LEGACY: free limited public preview; Meta never published first-party token prices.
rate_limit_headers: LIVE: x-ratelimit-limit-requests, x-ratelimit-remaining-requests, x-ratelimit-limit-tokens, x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens (no reset/retry-after header is documented). Limits apply per TEAM, not per key. Standard tier 3,000 RPM / 4,000,000 TPM; Contributor tier 100 RPM / 3,000,000 TPM; muse-image 150 RPM (no TPM); background /v1/responses submissions 600/min; transcribe 128 concurrent streams / 16,000 per hour. On 429 Meta says: exponential backoff with jitter, start ~500 ms and double per consecutive 429. LEGACY: advertised 3,000 RPM / 1,000,000 TPM across models; no rate-limit headers were documented; 429 body message was "You have exceeded the maximum number of tokens allowed within a given time frame. Wait a bit and try again."
reasoning_params: LIVE only (legacy Llama 3.3/4 had no reasoning controls). Chat Completions: reasoning_effort ∈ {"minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh"}; omitting it lets the model choose its own depth; "none" → HTTP 400 ("Muse Spark always reasons"). Reasoning text is NOT exposed in the Chat Completions response and is NOT persisted across turns — every turn re-reasons from scratch. Responses API: reasoning.effort (same values), reasoning summaries stream as response.reasoning_summary_text.delta; usage.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens; max_output_tokens includes reasoning; chain turns with previous_response_id (server keeps history, store defaults true) OR stateless replay via include:["reasoning.encrypted_content"] and echoing the encrypted reasoning items back as input (cannot combine with previous_response_id; reasoning items must precede assistant messages, function_call must pair with function_call_output). logprobs on any reasoning model → 400. Messages API: thinking {type:"adaptive"} or {type:"enabled", budget_tokens:n}; {type:"disabled"} → 400; output_config.effort ∈ low|medium|high|xhigh; usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens. For an agent harness Meta's own guidance is: use Responses (Codex uses wire_api="responses"; OpenCode should use @ai-sdk/openai with include:["reasoning.encrypted_content"], reasoningEffort "high"); Chat Completions "loses reasoning continuity across turns".
structured_output: LIVE Chat Completions: response_format:{type:"json_schema", json_schema:{name, schema, strict? (default false)}} — no json_object mode; sending text.format to Chat Completions → 400. Responses API uses text.format (same fields) instead of response_format. Messages API uses output_config.format. Decoding is constrained at generation time. strict:true subset (violations → 400 only when strict): root must be a plain object (no top-level anyOf/oneOf/allOf/enum/not); allOf and oneOf forbidden everywhere; anyOf allowed below root only; every object must set additionalProperties:false; required must list every key in properties; recursive/self-referencing schemas unsupported. Hard limits (all modes): nesting depth 10, 5,000 total properties, 120,000 chars of combined names/values, 1,000 enum values (enums with 250+ values capped at 15,000 chars), 200,000 expanded nodes. LEGACY: response_format {type:"json_schema", json_schema:{name, schema}} or {type:"text"}; the SDK exposed no strict flag on json_schema (strict existed only on tool functions).
usage_and_cost_in_response: No protocol returns cost; compute client-side from the hardcoded price table. LIVE Chat Completions: usage:{prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens} — cached/reasoning breakdowns are not documented on this surface (treat prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens / completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens as unverified). LIVE Responses: usage:{input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, input_tokens_details:{cached_tokens}, output_tokens_details:{reasoning_tokens}} — the only surface that reliably exposes both cached and reasoning counts for accurate billing. LIVE Messages: usage:{input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, output_tokens_details:{thinking_tokens}}. Billing rules: cached tokens billed at the cached-input rate, reasoning tokens at the output rate, "injected steering context" excluded; web_search billed per query outside usage. LEGACY native: metrics:[{metric: string, value: float, unit?: string}] (token counts; the exact metric names are no longer verifiable since the docs are gone); legacy compat returned OpenAI usage.
quirks: api.llama.com is dead: the Llama API public preview was retired 2026-07-06 and now returns a sunset response with redirect guidance; llama.developer.meta.com/docs/* 302-redirects to ai.developer.meta.com, whose /docs/api/*, /docs/features/compatibility, /docs/features/streaming, /docs/rate-limits and /docs/llama-api-deprecation pages 404 — the site now documents Meta Model API. Do not ship a provider that defaults to api.llama.com.

Meta Model API serves NO Llama models (only muse-spark-*, muse-image-1.0, muse-voice-transcribe-1.0, sam-3.1). If the harness wants Llama 3.3/4 it must route to Fireworks/OpenRouter/Groq/Bedrock; 'Llama 4'/'Llama 3' links on dev.meta.ai point to open-weight downloads, not API models.
Meta Model API is US-only public preview (developers in the US); expect 403/geo errors elsewhere.

tool_choice: only "auto" works on Chat Completions and Responses; "none", "required", and named function choices return HTTP 400. The harness must implement forced-tool / no-tool behaviour via prompting or by omitting tools, unlike OpenAI/Anthropic.

Function/tool names must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+$ with at most ONE dot; names with 2+ dots return 400 (MCP-style server.tool.sub names will fail — sanitize or wrap in a namespace tool). call_id must be 1–64 chars.
max_tokens is a deprecated alias — use max_completion_tokens on Chat Completions, max_output_tokens (minimum 16, includes reasoning tokens) on Responses, and the REQUIRED max_tokens on Messages.

reasoning_effort:"none" → 400 because Muse Spark always reasons; omit for model-chosen depth. Chat Completions never persists reasoning across turns (each turn re-thinks and re-bills); Responses with previous_response_id or include:["reasoning.encrypted_content"] is the only way to keep reasoning continuity — Meta's own coding-agent docs configure Codex/OpenCode on the Responses wire API for this reason.

Rejected params on Chat Completions (HTTP 400): n>1, stop, logprobs, logit_bias, prediction, web_search_options, modalities, audio, text.format. Rejected on Messages: stop_sequences, top_k, container, inference_geo, thinking:{type:"disabled"}, named tool_choice.

System prompt placement: Chat Completions accepts role "developer" (preferred) or "system" (identical priority); Responses uses the top-level `instructions` string (per request, not persisted); Messages uses top-level `system` (text blocks only).

Conversation validation is strict: malformed sequences (tool message without a matching preceding assistant tool_calls, function_call without function_call_output, reasoning items after assistant messages) return 400 instead of being repaired.

Strict JSON schema mode is opt-in (strict defaults false on both tools and response_format); arguments are only 'guided' by the schema when strict is false, so always validate tool arguments client-side. No json_object mode exists.

Streaming: Chat Completions ends with data: [DONE]; usage-in-stream (stream_options.include_usage) is NOT documented — verify live or count tokens client-side. Responses API stream uses named events (response.output_text.delta, response.function_call_arguments.delta, response.reasoning_summary_text.delta, response.completed/failed). background:true cannot be combined with stream:true; request bodies capped at 1 MiB.

Rate limits are per team (all keys share them) with headers x-ratelimit-{limit,remaining}-{requests,tokens} and no documented reset header; Standard 3,000 RPM / 4M TPM, Contributor 100 RPM / 3M TPM. Use jittered exponential backoff from ~500 ms on 429.

Pricing and context metadata are not in the API: hardcode $1.25/$0.15 cached/$4.25 per 1M for Standard muse-spark, $0.10/$0.002/$0.20 for -contributor (Meta may train on contributor prompts — surface that to users), 1,048,576 context, ~131,072 output cap. web_search costs $2.50 per 1k queries outside token usage.

Prompt caching is hint-based: prompt_cache_key groups requests, prompt_cache_retention "in_memory" | "24h"; cached-token counts are only exposed on Responses (input_tokens_details.cached_tokens) and Messages (cache_read_input_tokens), not documented on Chat Completions usage.

Anthropic-compat surface uses Authorization: Bearer (not x-api-key) and needs no anthropic-version header; for Claude Code set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.meta.ai (no /v1, no trailing slash), ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=$MODEL_API_KEY, and pin ANTHROPIC_MODEL / ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}_MODEL / CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL to muse-spark-1.3 to stop fallbacks to Claude model ids.

Model list contains non-chat models (muse-image-1.0, muse-voice-transcribe-1.0, sam-3.1) — filter the picker to ids starting with muse-spark. GET /v1/status is unauthenticated and useful for a connectivity probe; GET /v1/models validates the key.

Legacy-only gotchas if anyone still targets api.llama.com/v1: response is completion_message (not choices[]), stop_reason (not finish_reason), token counts in metrics[] (not usage), models list is a bare array, streaming uses event.event_type start/progress/complete/metrics with delta.type text|tool_call, and top_k / repetition_penalty were supported. The /compat/v1 path was the OpenAI-shaped alternative.
Key format for Meta Model API is LLM|<numeric app id>|<secret> — contains pipes, so quote it in shells and never split on '|' when parsing .env.
